title: Trim names and give blank greetings a friendly fallback

steps.title: Keep surrounding spaces out of a greeting
paragraphs: Calling `greet(" Ada ")` currently produces `"Hello,  Ada !"` because the supplied name goes into the message unchanged. We will trim it to produce `"Hello, Ada!"`, then give blank names the fallback `"Hello, friend!"`.
already accepts a name and returns a complete message. Keeping the cleanup inside that call means callers can continue supplying names in the same way.

steps.title: Trim the name in a small helper
paragraphs: Add `displayName` to remove spaces at the beginning and end of a name. Spaces between words remain, preserving names such as `"Mary Ann"`. For now, an all-space name becomes an empty string; the fallback comes after this helper is connected to the greeting.

The helper gives the cleanup its own name and lets `greet` concentrate on assembling the message. Keeping the expression directly in `greet` would be simpler for this small feature; the separate function makes the distinction explicit at the cost of another function to follow. Nothing calls it yet, so greetings still use the original name.

steps.title: Use the trimmed name and check the complete greeting
paragraphs: between `"Hello, "` and `"!"`. Now `" Ada "` becomes `"Ada"` before the greeting is assembled, so callers receive `"Hello, Ada!"` without cleaning up their inputs.

steps.title: Give blank names a friendly fallback
paragraphs: . That order matters: an all-space name becomes an empty string, so the helper returns `"friend"`. The greeting already calls this helper, so no further caller change is needed.

Extend the test with an all-space name and expect `"Hello, friend!"`. Together, the checks cover surrounding spaces, blank input, and a name with an internal space. The complete greeting now handles each case through the same call.
